items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Dule Ellington did at the Cotton Club in Harlem.

ctx.x: We recorded for a new record company called MGM which I think was affiliated with the movie company. This date was with the band and there were numbers where some vocals were done by Sy and Dickie Wells, Henri Wells and the whole orchestra. Sy was keen on the 'Glee Club Style' of singing and knew the technique of it. He had done it with the Lunceford orchestra successfully and on a few numbers with the Dorsey band. After two months at the Zanzibar, we finished in January 1947. As a rule, bands usually stayed in clubs of that standing for months no end and in some cases for years, as Dule Ellington did at the Cotton Club in Harlem. Charlie Johnson at Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ball room, which was a rare occasion for a dance hall, and numerous other orchestras that stayed in cabarets for six months and sometimes years.

There was another recording date before the band left the Zanzibar, but I don't remember if it was for MGM, but I do remember a couple of numbers we recorded. One was titled, "You can't tell the Depth of the Well by the length of the Handle on the Pump", a very long title, eh what! The other was "Bingle, Bangle, Bungle", and the words referred to a monkey who did not want to leave the jungle because modern civilization was too wild for him. I never saw or heard anything about that recording after it was made.
